ground_truth: The `totalEarnings` calculation in `vaultEndedWithdraw` is flawed because it fails to scale the `totalProtocolFee` to the current stETH/share ratio. This leads to an overestimation of earnings, causing early withdrawers to receive too much and leaving the vault insolvent for later users.

Incorrect accounting of protocol fees leads to double-charging users who withdraw early. This also causes a miscalculation and unfair distribution of the remaining earnings to other users, with some funds getting stuck in the contract.

The contract fails to correctly account for a slashing event that occurs after some users have already withdrawn earnings. It mixes pre-slashing share data with post-slashing asset values, which can cause final withdrawal transactions to revert and trap remaining funds.

After a slashing event, the contract incorrectly reduces its internal accounting of fixed deposits by the post-slashing value. If the stETH value recovers, this allows subsequent fixed-rate users to withdraw more than they deposited, profiting at the expense of variable-rate users.

An attacker can trigger a new Lido withdrawal request by sending a dust amount of stETH to the vault. If Lido is in "bunker mode", this will lock up all funds in the vault and create a Denial of Service for up to 36 days.
